summary:
Aurora Station is a browser game that puts kids aged 7 to 12 in command of a space station orbiting Mars for a 45-day mission. Players walk through a station modeled on the ISS, lead a crew of real NASA astronauts, and solve problems when things go wrong: a broken CO2 filter, a fire, an air leak, a solar storm.

Every decision has a cost. Each choice changes the station's food, water, oxygen, energy and radiation, and players learn that keeping people alive in space means trading one resource for another. The more than 80 missions are inspired by real events and studies, such as Apollo 13, the Mir fire, ISS repairs and NASA's CHAPEA Mars simulation, and each one ends with a real NASA fact. The game also uses live space weather data from NASA DONKI, so real solar storms can reach the station.

Accessibility was built in from the start: read-aloud, adjustable text size and speed, an easy-to-read font, full keyboard play and support for phones.

Aurora Station turns the challenges of future Mars missions into choices kids can understand, helping the next generation see themselves as explorers.
details:
What it does. Aurora Station is a story-driven management game. Players pick one of two commanders, meet their crew of real astronauts, and keep a Mars-orbiting station safe for 45 days across three acts: All Systems Go, Things Get Complicated and Survive.

How it works. Each day: an alarm rings and a red “!” shows the room; the player walks there and presses E; the mission window explains the problem in simple words; the player chooses; the five station meters change; a real NASA fact explains the science; a day summary closes the day. Choices can trigger later problems, so kids see that air, water, food and energy are connected.

Real NASA science. 10 missions based on real events (Apollo 13, Mir 1997, ISS 2004/2006/2008/2021, ESA Mars Express, CHAPEA 2025). Solar storms come from NASA DONKI (CMEs predicted to reach Mars, plus geomagnetic storms) via api.nasa.gov. When NASA can’t be reached, the game uses saved DONKI data and labels it NOT LIVE. The Credits screen lists every source.

Made for every kid. Read-aloud on every screen (L), big text and text-speed options, the Lexend font at 18 px or more, full keyboard play, 44 px buttons, visible focus, pause anytime, and layouts from monitors to phones. Danger is shown by color, blinking and written warnings, never color alone. Every screen was checked with axe-core (WCAG 2.2 AA).

Impact. Kids learn that resources in space are limited and linked, and that astronauts decide under uncertainty. Failure invites a new strategy instead of punishment. Works at home or in class.

Tools. Phaser 3, React 19, TypeScript, Zustand, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4, Web Speech API, Aseprite (hand-drawn characters), Vercel, Canva.
